questions.stem: A skydiver has just jumped from a plane and is accelerating downward. Which statement about the forces is correct?

options.text: Weight is greater than air resistance
Air resistance is greater than weight
Weight equals air resistance
Only weight acts on the skydiver

questions.explanation: If the skydiver is accelerating downward, there must be a resultant downward force. This means weight (downward) is greater than air resistance (upward). Option (c) would mean zero resultant force and constant velocity (terminal velocity). Option (d) ignores air resistance, which acts on all objects moving through air. As the skydiver speeds up, air resistance increases until it equals weight — that is when terminal velocity is reached.

questions.stem: A car travels at constant velocity along a level road. The driving force from the engine is 1200 N. What is the total resistive force (friction and drag)?

options.text: 0 N

questions.explanation: At constant velocity, the resultant force is zero (Newton's First Law). This means the driving force exactly equals the total resistive force: 1200 N. Option (a) would mean no friction at all, which is impossible on a road. Option (d) would mean the resistive forces exceed the driving force, causing deceleration.

questions.stem: Why do skydivers reach a higher terminal velocity when falling in a streamlined position compared to a spread-eagle position?

options.text: Their weight is greater in a streamlined position
A streamlined position has less surface area, so air resistance is lower and they must go faster for drag to equal weight
Gravity is stronger in a streamlined position
The air is thinner in a streamlined position

questions.explanation: Terminal velocity occurs when air resistance equals weight. A streamlined position reduces the cross-sectional area, which reduces air resistance at any given speed. So the skydiver must fall faster before drag builds up enough to equal their weight. Their weight stays the same regardless of body position. This is why the spread-eagle position is used to slow down.

questions.stem: A box is pushed across a rough floor at constant speed using a horizontal force of 80 N. The box is then placed on a smoother floor. Using the same 80 N force, what happens?

options.text: The box moves at the same constant speed
The box decelerates
The box accelerates because friction is now less than the applied force
The box does not move

questions.explanation: On the rough floor, 80 N exactly balanced friction (constant speed). On the smoother floor, friction is less than 80 N, so there is now a resultant forward force, causing acceleration. The box speeds up until friction (which increases with speed if drag is involved) once again balances the 80 N force at a new, higher constant speed.

questions.stem: Friction between shoes and the ground is essential for walking. Without friction, what would happen when you try to push backward with your foot?

options.text: You would walk normally
You would walk faster because there is no resistance
Your foot would slip backward and you would not move forward
You would jump upward instead

questions.explanation: Walking works because your foot pushes backward on the ground, and friction pushes forward on your foot (Newton's Third Law). Without friction, your foot would simply slide backward — like trying to walk on very slippery ice. This shows that friction is not always undesirable; it is essential for grip, walking, and driving.
